content.text:
The migrated file is at `out/module.ts`. It type-checks, its outputs match the original on every input I tested, and the bundle drops from 12,330 to 2,164 bytes (min+gzip).

**Result**

| | Original (lodash) | Migrated (es-toolkit) |
|---|---|---|
| Bundle, min+gzip | 12,330 B | 2,164 B |
| Own code bytes | 182 B | 103 B |
| `tsc -p .` | passes | passes |

**Function choices**

- **`toSlug`** uses `es-toolkit/compat/kebabCase`. The main `es-toolkit/string` `kebabCase` looked equivalent on a first sample, but a larger run showed it diverges from lodash on about 0.06% of inputs in the stated range, for example `m41STkXkL.K` gives `m-41-s-tk-xk-l-k` instead of `m-41st-k-xk-l-k`. The compat version matched lodash on all 300,000 random inputs. It accounts for most of the size (about 1.6 KB, mainly the `deburr` code it pulls in).
- **`byNameKey`** uses `keyBy` from `es-toolkit/array`. The es-toolkit version takes a function rather than a property name, so the call uses a one-line adapter, `(row) => row.name`. It keeps the last row per name, as lodash does.
- **`preview`** uses `es-toolkit/compat/truncate`. es-toolkit has no non-compat `truncate`, and the compat version takes the same `{ length }` options shape, so no adapter is needed.

No lodash import remains, nothing was installed, and no other files were created in the project. The only file in `out/` is `module.ts`.

**Checks**

- The bundled original and migrated modules agree on the example inputs and on 120,006 random inputs drawn from the stated ranges. The random inputs are my own generator, not an exhaustive check.
- The ~2 KB bundle is larger than it would be with the main es-toolkit `kebabCase`, but that version gives wrong slugs, so I kept the compat function.
